description: Runs email campaigns and maintains audience and engagement records.
access_note: Account owners can generate a key. Free Marketing accounts have sending and contact limits. Use OAuth2 for installations by other customers.
blocker: No material barrier to a single-account read prototype. Customer installs require OAuth2.
toolkit: Start with audience counts and campaign reporting.
unknowns: Verify account-level MCP coverage separately from documentation search.

sources.note: Own-account keys and delegated OAuth2 tokens can travel via Basic or Bearer authentication.
Marketing v3 generally follows REST conventions.
The account setup guide links key generation with audience, campaign and analytics functions and ties available operations to plan.
The pricing comparison includes a free plan with send limits.
Mailchimp documents a credential-free marketing documentation MCP. This particular server searches docs only.
Pipedream lists an independently operated MCP connection for marketing accounts.

description: Manages customer profiles, marketing campaigns and event-driven messaging.
access_note: A test account starts on the free plan. Owners, administrators or managers may manage keys. Public directory listing has a separate review.
blocker: Free test accounts support scoped prototypes. Directory publication adds review.
toolkit: Read campaign and segment summaries with a scoped key.
unknowns: Check which send operations are enabled on the target plan.

sources.note: Klaviyo separates private server keys, delegated OAuth and public client IDs, and lists the roles allowed to manage keys.
New integration test accounts begin on the free plan and inherit its usage limits.
The developer guide distinguishes testing from submitting a public integration to the directory.
The API reference describes JSON:API resource relationships, includes, sparse fields and pagination.
Klaviyo documents hosted and local MCP modes and lists campaign, event, profile, list, and segment scopes.
Pipedream publishes a Klaviyo OAuth MCP connection.

description: Combines funnels, contacts, courses and marketing automation.
access_note: Account settings issue public API keys. The vendor explicitly includes MCP on its free plan and caps public API keys at three per account.
blocker: The account owner can create a public key. Three keys per account limits environment separation.
toolkit: Start with contact search and tags. The vendor MCP already covers these operations.
unknowns: Check plan entitlements for advanced raw API endpoints separately from MCP.

sources.note: The API guide shows generating a named key, the three-key cap, and supported contact, offer, product and booking operations.
The company's MCP product page confirms all plans, including Free, can connect.
Pipedream documents its separate Systeme.io MCP connection.

description: Lets users discover and save visual content and advertisers measure campaigns.
access_note: Pinterest approves Trial access. Standard access requires review of a video and the OAuth flow. Trial-created content is creator-visible only.
blocker: Pinterest must approve the application, and Trial pins and boards cannot be published visibly to others.
toolkit: Validate pin analytics in an approved trial, then request Standard before launching publishing.
unknowns: Check the exact tools approved for the partner MCP account.

sources.note: The access table lists ads, analytics, boards and catalogs. Trial and Standard have distinct review and visibility rules.
The sandbox shows resource-oriented HTTP methods on v5 pins and boards.
Pinterest publishes a remote MCP server and connection URL.
The company announcement identifies approved partners as the audience for its MCP.
Pipedream publishes a separately operated Pinterest MCP connection.

description: Publishes and analyzes short-form social posts on Meta's Threads network.
access_note: Create a Meta app and authorize a Threads test user. Access beyond eligible roles can require permission review. A universal fee-free entitlement was not established.
blocker: Testing with app roles does not establish authorization to act for external users.
toolkit: Prototype read-only insights with an authorized test account before requesting production permissions.
unknowns: Confirm the exact review requirements for the chosen Threads scopes.

sources.note: Meta's own Postman collection walks through creating a Threads app, user authorization and tokens, then exercises its Graph API for posts and insights.
Meta documents role-based testing for business apps and advanced permissions reviewed before release.
The andreaselmi repository documents a community Threads MCP for publishing, reading posts and fetching insights.

description: Provides email delivery APIs for transactional messages and marketing campaigns.
access_note: The account can start with a 60-day trial of the Email API and Marketing Campaigns. Account verification and continued service requirements apply.
blocker: The documented trial expires. Production sending also requires appropriate sender verification.
toolkit: Start with account statistics and a restricted key. Validate sender identity before enabling send actions.
unknowns: Check sending limits and the paid tier needed after the trial.

sources.note: The v3 Mail Send endpoint accepts a JSON body and expects the SendGrid API key as a bearer credential.
The first scoped or revocable key is created in the SendGrid app.
Twilio describes a 60-day SendGrid trial and account verification.
Twilio lists email sending, campaign measurement and inbound processing.
Pipedream publishes a SendGrid MCP connection for its integration platform.
The vendor explicitly identifies v3 as a REST interface.
Official request documentation lists supported language SDKs.

description: Provides storefront and merchant APIs for operating online shops.
access_note: Partners can create free dev stores for testing with no live transactions. Real merchant access requires an install with appropriate scopes.
blocker: A development store is enough for catalog prototyping. Merchant authorization is required for real data.
toolkit: Use GraphQL Admin API for catalog and inventory reads in a dev store.
unknowns: Confirm requirements for protected customer data before requesting those scopes.

sources.note: Shopify identifies OAuth-issued tokens for Admin GraphQL and lists product, order, customer and inventory data.
The Partner glossary defines a dev store as free for testing, with no live selling.
Shopify's hosted Shop MCP serves shopper discovery and checkout. Its scope differs from Admin API.
Shopify separately ships a local developer MCP for documentation and tooling.
The REST Admin API is legacy. Shopify requires GraphQL Admin API for all new public apps.
Pipedream publishes its own Shopify store MCP connection.

description: Adds an open-source ecommerce store and administration APIs to WordPress.
access_note: A developer can install the free plugin locally and issue REST keys for a WordPress user. The chosen user's permissions govern access.
blocker: Access to a WordPress installation and permission to issue keys are required.
toolkit: Expose read-only orders and product lookup on a local test shop.
unknowns: Check the deployed plugin version and MCP adapter before promising MCP compatibility.

sources.note: WooCommerce describes its free, open-source plugin and installation process.
The authentication guide explains scoped consumer key/secret pairs, HTTPS Basic and an alternative OAuth 1.0a flow.
The v3 REST API uses HTTP verbs and JSON to read or change WooCommerce data.
The official developer preview exposes product and order abilities through a separately installed WordPress MCP Adapter.
The Woo marketplace documents w7s's separate MCP extension and credential settings.

description: Provides store management and storefront APIs for ecommerce merchants.
access_note: Developers can register a free portal account and build on a trial store with install privileges. Marketplace submission requires an approved Technology Partner.
blocker: A trial supports prototyping. Marketplace distribution requires BigCommerce partner approval.
toolkit: Prototype catalog reads on a trial store. Budget a separate step for marketplace distribution.
unknowns: Check individual sandbox and plan limits for high-volume integrations.

sources.note: Developer quick start distinguishes storefront GraphQL, checkout apps and store data management over REST and GraphQL.
BigCommerce describes three OAuth-based account types with different credential scopes.
The tutorial permits a trial store with install rights and a free developer account.
An approved Technology Partner account is required for app marketplace submission.
Vendor documentation distinguishes the docs server, Storefront MCP and store management abilities.
BigCommerce advertises a fully functional 15-day free trial.
Pipedream publishes a separately operated BigCommerce MCP.

description: Offers shopper-facing commerce and backend merchandising APIs for Salesforce B2C Commerce.
access_note: SCAPI is included for B2C Commerce customers. A demo sandbox illustrates shopper calls, while tenant admin access needs Account Manager registration and roles.
blocker: A demo shopper call cannot grant the tenant-specific admin role required by a merchant toolkit.
toolkit: Use the demo for catalog reads, then obtain an authorized merchant tenant for admin tools.
unknowns: Identify an entitled organization and delegated administrator for live merchant workflows.

sources.note: The SCAPI guide describes REST, a demo product call, B2C customer entitlements, and a vendor MCP that executes Admin APIs.
Admin clients register in Account Manager and exchange client credentials for an access token.
The release notes distinguish OAuth 2.1 shopper access and refresh tokens.
The role guide directs users without an Account Manager account to their account administrator.

description: Offers modular ecommerce APIs for Adobe Commerce and self-hosted Magento Open Source.
access_note: Magento Open Source can be installed locally. An administrator authorizes integration permissions. Adobe Commerce cloud authentication and entitlements differ.
blocker: A local Magento installation supports prototyping. Installation and permissions must match the target edition.
toolkit: Prototype catalog reads on Magento Open Source and treat Adobe Commerce cloud as a separate deployment target.
unknowns: Check edition-specific authentication and endpoint parity before cloud rollout.

sources.note: The project manifest identifies Magento Open Source and its open-source licenses.
Adobe's web API overview lists REST, SOAP and GraphQL for commerce service integrations.
The integration flow uses OAuth 1.0a, with authorization in the store. It is recorded under Other.
The GraphQL guide explains role-specific authorization tokens and product and category access.
Adobe documents MCP tooling for extension development and cloud migrations. This covers developer work, not storefront orders.
Adobe's marketplace identifies miniOrange as the publisher of a Magento store MCP.

description: Provides APIs for Squarespace merchants to manage store operations.
access_note: Owners can create site-bound API keys. Commerce endpoint access varies by plan, including orders on Core, Plus, Advanced and legacy Commerce Advanced.
blocker: The merchant plan determines which Commerce API permissions can be issued.
toolkit: Start with product and order lookups for merchants whose plan supports the required scopes.
unknowns: Check OAuth extension registration and exact permissions on the merchant's current or legacy plan.

sources.note: The Commerce API overview maps inventory adjustments, product resources and order history.
The product reference accepts API keys or OAuth access tokens in the Bearer authorization header.
Squarespace lists the eligible plans for generating keys and accessing individual Commerce APIs.
Vendor MCP tools include looking up orders, editing products and managing site contacts.
Pipedream lists a separately operated Squarespace MCP connection.

description: Provides merchant stores and a programmable ecommerce platform under Lightspeed.
access_note: The developer guide says only paid stores can access the API. Eligible test stores may request a free upgrade by email.
blocker: A free test-store upgrade is request-based. Production API access requires a paid store.
toolkit: Start with inventory lookup on an eligible test store or a merchant-authorized paid store.
unknowns: Confirm eligibility and turnaround for a free test-store upgrade.

sources.note: Ecwid requires a paid store and lists the criteria and email route for complimentary test-store upgrades.
The first-request walkthrough uses OAuth2, store-specific tokens and a Bearer header to access REST.
The reference covers store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings.

description: Lets creators sell digital products, manage customers and track sales.
access_note: Create an app in a seller account and generate a personal token. Other sellers authorize with OAuth. The platform has no monthly fee and charges per transaction.
blocker: The owner token supports prototyping. Customer installations need a working OAuth redirect.
toolkit: Start with product, sale and license lookups, keeping seller data isolated per OAuth grant.
unknowns: Confirm the scopes required for any changes to memberships or products.

sources.note: Account settings can generate a token, the example calls the products HTTP endpoint, and external users authorize via code exchange for a bearer token.
The pricing page charges transaction fees and states there is no monthly charge.
Gumroad documents its license verification HTTP endpoint.
Gumroad's CLI lists product, sales and other seller resources and documents OAuth sign-in.
Gumroad publishes its Cursor connector's MCP address and describes access to sales, products and payouts.
Pipedream publishes a separate Gumroad MCP integration.

description: Lets developers build tools for Amazon seller and vendor operations.
access_note: Developers register and request roles. Public apps need Amazon approval, an Appstore listing and seller authorization. Private registration is separate.
blocker: Amazon must approve public distribution and data roles before a multi-seller toolkit can operate.
toolkit: Use model definitions for development and secure public developer approval before testing seller-specific workflows.
unknowns: Confirm current public developer fees and restricted role policies for the intended use case.

sources.note: The onboarding guide distinguishes private and public applications, seller OAuth2 and marketplace approval, and lists operational REST domains.
Amazon describes REST access to orders, shipments, payments and product data.
Amazon publishes the official SDK specifically for the REST SP-API.
Amazon's seller toolkit identifies its Selling Partner Connector as the MCP behind the skills and describes approval of write actions.
Amazon also publishes local sample SP-API developer-assistant MCPs, separately from the selling partner connector.

description: Provides creator checkout and payment infrastructure, rebranded from FanBasis to Commas.
access_note: FanBasis documents a sandbox and a signup form. The sources do not establish automatic key issuance or whether the replacement brand imposes a paid or approval gate.
blocker: The documented checkout API is technically usable, but eligibility for a fresh Commas sandbox key is unresolved.
toolkit: A checkout-session wrapper is technically plausible after Commas confirms current credentials and endpoints.
unknowns: Does a new developer receive a sandbox key without sales or payment?
Which legacy checkout endpoints are supported for new Commas accounts?

sources.note: Commas confirms the July 2026 name change and identifies FanBasis, Inc. as its operator.
The vendor's embedded-checkout reference shows an HTTP POST with x-api-key to create a checkout session, with separate sandbox and production examples.
The vendor documents its payment checkout SDK and separate sandbox and production settings.
The legacy onboarding form asks for business and website information. It does not promise API credentials.

description: Supplies search rankings, keywords, backlinks and business data through APIs.
access_note: Register to see API credentials and receive a small one-time live testing balance. The free sandbox provides test data. Live use beyond credit is metered.
blocker: The trial balance is finite and sandbox results cannot validate live data quality.
toolkit: Start with one keyword or SERP lookup and expose an explicit cost estimate before bulk jobs.
unknowns: Check the credit cost and freshness for the chosen endpoints.

sources.note: The v3 authentication guide specifies HTTP Basic using the API login and password.
Trial registration provides dashboard credentials and a finite live balance. A free sandbox handles larger test volumes.
The vendor catalogs SERP, keyword, backlinks and business data APIs.
DataForSEO documents how to connect its own MCP server using the same API credentials.
Pipedream separately publishes an MCP connection for DataForSEO.

description: Provides search and backlink datasets and tools for monitoring SEO projects.
access_note: The standalone API offers a 14-day credit-limited trial with MCP access. Ongoing production consumption requires credits.
blocker: Credits and trial expiry constrain repeated SEO analysis.
toolkit: Prototype keyword and backlink summaries with credit tracking.
unknowns: Verify which Project API operations are included in the chosen package.

sources.note: The dashboard issues an API key. Data API examples use a Token header and JSON HTTP requests for backlink and subscription endpoints.
The pricing page documents the standalone trial, credits, MCP access, and keyword, backlink, AI search and audit data.
The knowledge base describes the vendor's MCP connecting assistants to its SEO data.

description: Provides keyword, backlink, ranking and site-audit intelligence.
access_note: Core SEO data requires a qualifying subscription and uses API units. A small public subset and special test requests are free. Only workspace owners/admins manage API keys.
blocker: Free public or test endpoints cannot deliver unrestricted, fresh competitor research.
toolkit: Offer feature-scoped keyword and backlink lookups for customers with sufficient API units.
unknowns: Check the exact datasets, row limits and units for the customer's subscription.

sources.note: Workspace owners and admins create v3 keys and set usage limits.
Ahrefs Connect documents OAuth testing, the v3 SEO resource groups and the per-request unit model.
Ahrefs compares subscription capabilities including direct API access and the shared pool of API units.
The official reference explicitly identifies a limited set of free public endpoints.
Ahrefs documents a hosted MCP for Lite and higher plan workspaces.
Pipedream lists a separate Ahrefs MCP connection.

description: Runs web extraction jobs and returns structured results.
access_note: A developer can create an account and obtain an API token. The free plan includes a monthly quota without a credit card. OAuth2 is documented for an MCP transport.
blocker: The free quota supports a small prototype. MCP transport and raw API support different operations.
toolkit: Expose a single bounded fetch and result lookup using the documented free allowance.
unknowns: Confirm whether a selected operation belongs to the legacy scraper API or the current MCP toolset.

sources.note: The HTTP API authenticates requests with API tokens and documents a results endpoint.
MrScraper documents an endpoint to run an existing scraper on a supplied URL.
The pricing page describes monthly free scraper credits without a card.
The vendor MCP guide lists supported tools, removes legacy operations, and documents OAuth 2.1 or bearer keys for applicable HTTP deployments.

description: Runs cloud automation programs called Actors and stores their datasets and results.
access_note: Free accounts receive a monthly usage allowance without a card. Console users can create a token; individual Actors have their own pricing.
blocker: A free account supports bounded runs. Actor-specific fees and input costs vary.
toolkit: Start with Actor discovery, status polling and dataset pagination using a scoped token.
unknowns: Check the Actor's price and permission manifest before enabling a run.

sources.note: The v2 reference documents bearer tokens, REST endpoints, storage and official API clients.
The vendor's integration guide describes OAuth for connecting external users to Apify.
The agent quickstart describes free credits, token creation and running Actors through the Apify MCP.
Pricing distinguishes the platform allowance from individual Actor pricing models.
Pipedream documents a separately operated Apify MCP connection.

description: Turns public web pages and sites into searchable and structured content.
access_note: A free account receives monthly credits. A separately limited keyless route supports a subset of operations. Authenticated use unlocks broader coverage.
blocker: Keyless daily quotas restrict the initial toolset. An account key enables crawl and map.
toolkit: Start with keyless page reads and search. Add an account key for full-site crawl.
unknowns: Confirm credit costs for requested extraction formats and hosted operation limits.

sources.note: The crawl product page describes the API key path, free account credits and site-level crawling.
Official rate-limit documentation explicitly lists keyless support for the REST API, CLI and SDKs, and identifies operations requiring a key.
The Firecrawl docs repository distinguishes keyless MCP from the endpoint accepting Bearer authentication.
Pipedream publishes a separately operated Firecrawl MCP connection.

description: Provides web data collection, extraction and search services.
access_note: The official Web MCP offers a capped free allowance without a card. This entitlement is specific to MCP; direct datasets and other REST products have separate terms.
blocker: The free MCP provides a concrete prototype path. Entitlements for separate API products must be confirmed.
toolkit: Reuse Bright Data's free MCP for a bounded search or page read.
unknowns: Confirm independent dataset API pricing before expanding beyond the Web MCP.

sources.note: The scraper management reference demonstrates a dataset snapshot status HTTP request using an API key as a bearer token.
Bright Data's own documentation identifies its Web MCP and free tier.
The publisher's MCP repository outlines account token setup, a no-card quota, search, page extraction and structured scrapers.

description: An open-source command-line project that checks public account names across services.
access_note: The CLI runs locally without a vendor account. A separate project-owned REST wrapper requires local installation and hosting. No maintained public hosted endpoint was verified.
blocker: There is no verified hosted API with a service guarantee. The local wrapper and underlying external sites require maintenance.
toolkit: Use a local, opt-in brand-handle availability skill. Treat website matches as unverified until confirmed.
unknowns: Whether the self-hosted REST wrapper is currently maintained and production-compatible.
Authentication for a hosted deployment depends on the operator.

sources.note: The upstream README documents a local open-source CLI and export options. Its main invocation does not call for a Sherlock account or key.
The same project's separate MIT-licensed repository describes a Django REST server run on localhost. It does not promise a hosted public API.
An independent PyPI publisher documents a local MCP distribution that includes a Sherlock adapter.

description: Enriches business contacts and companies using multiple data providers.
access_note: The published onboarding route starts with a call, a benchmark, quoted terms and signing. Results consume credits; an empty result can be free.
blocker: Published rates and production onboarding depend on a benchmark and vendor conversation.
toolkit: Request a sandbox key and terms for a narrow enrichment use case before planning a rollout.
unknowns: Is there an alternate self-serve developer sandbox?
Which API-key header applies to each API version?

sources.note: The product page shows a contact enrichment POST with x-api-key and a follow-up GET for job results.
The Prospector page documents domain and role filters with a key-authenticated request.
Pricing describes outcome-based credits, with rates quoted after a benchmark.
The onboarding page starts with a call, followed by a benchmark and signing before go-live.

description: Searches and enriches B2B data and automates go-to-market workflows.
access_note: Clay's current developer platform includes Free accounts and basic table reads. Structured queries require Enterprise table sync, and free search results are capped. MCP uses a separate workspace-approved client.
blocker: The free developer API supports bounded search and reads. Advanced table queries and MCP permissions have separate gates.
toolkit: Build a basic workspace search or enrichment wrapper. Keep table writes and advanced queries out of the initial scope.
unknowns: Check per-workspace client allowlists for MCP and provider credit costs.

sources.note: Clay distinguishes an API key and CLI session, includes Free developer API access, restricts table writes, and reserves advanced table sync for Enterprise.
Clay documents hosted MCP, dynamic OAuth client registration, bearer access tokens and workspace client restrictions.
The account guide describes generating a personal key for Clay-native data tools.

description: Hosts repositories, issues, pull requests and developer collaboration workflows.
access_note: A free personal account can create access tokens. Some public REST reads require no authentication. Organization policies, SSO and repository scopes govern private access.
blocker: Public or owned repositories are enough to prototype. Organization access may require approval.
toolkit: Start with read-only issue and pull-request status. Use installation-scoped permissions for organizations.
unknowns: Check target organization policies and scopes before private repository access.

sources.note: GitHub documents personal tokens, app tokens, workflow tokens and limited app endpoints accepting Basic authentication.
The getting-started guide distinguishes public unauthenticated requests from token-authorized REST access.
GitHub's GraphQL guide accepts personal tokens, GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.
GitHub Free supports personal accounts with public and private repositories.
GitHub's official MCP repository documents toolsets for repository contents, issues and pull requests.
Pipedream offers a separately operated GitHub MCP integration.

description: Builds, deploys and manages web applications and project domains.
access_note: A personal Hobby account can create access tokens and supports personal, noncommercial projects. Team operations need appropriate team scope and entitlement.
blocker: Personal test projects support the prototype. Commercial projects and team features have different terms.
toolkit: Expose deployment status and project discovery with an account-scoped token.
unknowns: Confirm the commercial plan and team role required for the production use case.

sources.note: The REST reference documents token generation in account settings, Bearer requests, the SDK and deployments, domains and environment settings.
Vercel identifies Hobby as its personal, noncommercial plan.
The Hobby guide identifies a free development plan.
Vercel documents a remote OAuth-protected MCP for authenticated project operations and public tools.
Pipedream publishes its own token-authenticated Vercel MCP integration.

description: Builds and deploys sites and manages their hosting, DNS and form submissions.
access_note: Free includes API-based deployment within the included credit allowance. Users can generate expiring personal tokens. SAML team data has an additional authorization option.
blocker: A free personal project supports build-status lookups. Production deploys consume plan credits and require appropriate site access.
toolkit: Start with deploy status and previews. Put production deployment behind a separate permission.
unknowns: Confirm team SAML authorization and current credits before enabling production deployments.

sources.note: The REST guide documents site/deploy/DNS/form capabilities, OAuth2 and personal Bearer token creation.
The pricing guide includes free accounts and deployment by API in its credit-based offering.
Netlify documents connecting clients to its remote MCP for deployment workflows.
Pipedream publishes a separate Netlify MCP connection.

description: Provides networking, DNS, edge compute and storage APIs.
access_note: Users can create a free account and issue scoped user API tokens. OAuth clients require permission to create them, and resource operations remain plan-specific.
blocker: A free account supports a scoped prototype. Access to a specific zone or product depends on its role and plan.
toolkit: Start with read-only DNS or zone analytics and reuse the native MCP for discovery.
unknowns: Verify plan-appropriate GraphQL datasets before promising analytics fields.

sources.note: The API overview covers personal token creation, legacy API keys, permissions and official SDKs.
Cloudflare illustrates its v4 HTTP resource operations and Bearer authentication.
Cloudflare documents creating Free accounts and managing account access.
The vendor documents creating an OAuth client with account-level permission.
Cloudflare provides GraphQL schemas for DNS analytics.
Cloudflare documents its own API MCP with access to DNS, Workers, R2 and other product operations.
Pipedream publishes an independent Cloudflare MCP integration.

description: Provides hosted Postgres, data APIs and developer services for applications.
access_note: Free organizations can provision projects. Project data keys and Management API personal/OAuth tokens serve different purposes. Database policies still control row access.
blocker: A free project supports test data. The connector must distinguish project keys from management tokens and respect database policies.
toolkit: Prototype read-only table access on a sample project and request management scopes only for administrative tools.
unknowns: Check row-level security and project-scoped permissions before exposing live customer tables.

sources.note: The billing guide describes the Free plan and its project limits.
Supabase documents the project REST endpoint and database grants that control exposed objects.
The API keys guide explains publishable and secret project credentials.
The official documentation describes the GraphQL database interface.
The Management API reference distinguishes personal access tokens and delegated OAuth credentials.
Supabase identifies its official MCP as an interface for connecting development tools.
Pipedream publishes a separate Supabase MCP integration.

description: Stores connected data in a graph database queried with Cypher.
access_note: AuraDB Free provides a no-card hosted database, and developers can install locally. Database login and Aura management credentials are separate.
blocker: A free database supports HTTP Cypher reads. Instance management uses a separate identity.
toolkit: Start with parameterized, read-only graph queries using the database Query API or official MCP.
unknowns: Confirm Aura management API plan eligibility separately from database query access.

sources.note: Neo4j's Query API executes Cypher statements over HTTP on a local or hosted server.
The database Query API supports Basic and Bearer authentication.
The Aura platform authentication guide documents client ID/secret exchange for an OAuth access token. This is separate from the database login.
The Aura platform reference provides instance management endpoints.
AuraDB Free is a managed database with no credit card required.
Neo4j describes vendor-hosted MCP availability on Free and other Aura tiers.

description: Provides cloud data warehousing, SQL execution and managed database resources.
access_note: The self-service trial provides limited credits for storage and compute. SQL, resource APIs and managed MCP operate under account roles and grants.
blocker: A trial can validate a prototype, but regular warehouse queries require ongoing compute and data privileges.
toolkit: Prototype read-only sample-data queries with bounded result sizes and a limited warehouse.
unknowns: Check grants for MCP objects and the account's compute budget before production use.

sources.note: Snowflake documents OAuth, key-pair JWTs, programmatic access tokens and workload identity federation.
The SQL REST API submits statements and accesses or updates data.
Snowflake provides REST tutorials for database, schema and other resource-object management.
The self-service trial guide explains limited usage credits and storage and compute consumption.
Snowflake documents its managed MCP server and role privileges required to use it.
Pipedream publishes a separately operated Snowflake MCP connection.
